title: The targeted project request — question explanation
learningObjective: Use context, relationship and business-process checks to detect targeted deception
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: A message uses your real project name and mentions a current deadline. It asks you to open a shared document and sign in again, but the sender domain differs from the partner’s known domain.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Use context, relationship and business-process checks to detect targeted deception
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option A: Verify the request with the partner using a previously established contact channel, and access the project system independently. Use relationship and workflow context as signals, but authenticate through an independent channel.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option B: Changing devices does not make a deceptive link or credential prompt trustworthy. Option C: A response goes to the potentially compromised sender and does not independently verify the request. Option D: Public or compromised information can make targeted deception convincing; context alone is not authentication.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Pause the sign-in request, contact the partner through known contact details, and report the mismatch to the security team. Targeted content can be accurate and still fraudulent; independently verify the sender and workflow.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
